children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares fell on Wednesday on concerns over high bond yields, posting their biggest quarterly drop in 6-1/2 years.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed down 32.77 points, or 0.48%, at 6,838.04, trimming early gains of more than 1%.
** The KOSPI fell 19.3% this quarter, marking its biggest quarterly loss since the first quarter of 2020, after rising for six consecutive quarters. It has still risen 62.3% so far this year.

** US stocks ended slightly lower on Tuesday, as government bond yields continued their ascent ahead of inflation and labour market data, while investors assessed comments from Federal Reserve officials for the path of interest rates.
** "There was caution ahead of major events, such as US inflation data and Micron Technology's
earnings," said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.
** South Korea will report its monthly trade figures for September on Thursday.
** South Korea's finance minister said authorities were closely monitoring bond markets and would take market-stabilising measures if bond yields rose excessively.
** South Korea's factory output unexpectedly fell in August, data showed.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 1.47%, while peer SK Hynix
gained 0.62%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 1.28%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 1.43% and 2.76%, respectively.
** Of the total 914 traded issues, 352 shares advanced, while 513 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 2.1 trillion won ($1.55 billion).
** The won was quoted at 1,352.8 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.09% higher than its previous close at 1,354.0.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 6.9 basis points to 4.003%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 7.3 basis points to 4.397%.
